title: Git in the editor
summary: Where your changes show up, how to commit them, and which branch you're on.

say.never: **Git** is a tool that remembers every version of your work, like unlimited save points in a game. The editor has it built in, under the **Source Control** icon. We'll make your first save point together: I'll point, you click. You can still use the editor and terminal normally while I'm here.
say.bit: The editor has git built in. Let's make your first commit together: I'll point, you do it. The editor and terminal work normally while I'm here.

say.never: Each numbered folder in this lesson is its own **repository**, which is just a project folder that git is watching. Each one gets its own section in Source Control. Start with **01-first-commit**.
say.bit: Each numbered folder in this lesson is its own repository, so each one gets its own section here. Start with **01-first-commit**.

say.never: Click the **Explorer**, the top icon on the left, and open the file `01-first-commit/roster.txt`. Click the folder name to open it, then click the file.
say.bit: Go to the **Explorer** (the top icon) and open `01-first-commit/roster.txt`.

say.never: Add your name on a new line, then save with **Ctrl+S**. The Source Control icon now shows a number. That's how many files you've changed since your last save point.
say.bit: Add your name on a new line, then press **Ctrl+S** to save. The Source Control icon will show a number: that's how many files you've changed.

hint.never: add your name and press Ctrl+S.
hint.bit: add your name and press Ctrl+S.

say.never: Click the **Source Control** icon again to look at your change.
say.bit: Open Source Control again to see your change.

say.never: There's your file. The letter **M** means *modified*: it's different from the last save point. Click it to see exactly what changed, old on the left and new on the right.
say.bit: There it is. **M** means modified. Click it to see exactly what changed, side by side.

say.never: **Staging** means choosing which changes go into the next save point. It's like putting items in a box before you seal it. Hover over `roster.txt` and press the **+** to put it in the box.
say.bit: **Staging** picks what goes into the next commit. Hover over `roster.txt` and press the **+**.

say.never: Type a short message saying what you changed, like `Add my name to the roster`, then press **Commit**. A **commit** is a saved snapshot of your work, plus your note about it. Write the note for a teammate who'll read it next month.
say.bit: Type a message saying what you changed, like `Add my name to the roster`, then press **Commit**. A commit is a saved snapshot of your work.

hint.never: write a message and press Commit.
hint.bit: write a message and press Commit.

say.never: Your commit is now at the top of the **Graph**, which is the history. It shows who made the commit, when, and the message you wrote. Every commit stays there forever, so you can always go back.
say.bit: Your commit is now at the top of the **Graph**: who made it, when, and your message.

say.never: A **branch** is your own separate line of work. The bottom-left corner shows which branch you're on. Click it to switch branches or make a new one. Our branches are named like `issue-12-add-turbo-boost`, which says what the work is for.
say.bit: The bottom-left corner always shows your current branch. Click it to switch branches or make a new one. Our feature branches are named like `issue-12-add-turbo-boost`.

say.never: Everything you just clicked can also be done by typing commands in the **terminal**. Open it with **Ctrl** and the backtick key (above **Tab**).
say.bit: Everything here can be done by typing git commands too.

hint.never: press Ctrl and the backtick key (above Tab).

say.never: Type `cd 01-first-commit` and press **Enter**. That moves into the folder. Then type `git log --oneline` and press **Enter**. It lists your commits, and yours is the first line.
say.bit: Type `cd 01-first-commit`, press Enter, then `git log --oneline`. Your commit is the first line.

say.never: Each numbered folder has a `README.md` with the next task: a feature branch, a merge, a conflict and a rebase. Check your progress by clicking the lesson chip at the top of the screen.
say.bit: Each numbered folder's `README.md` has the next task: a feature branch, a merge, a conflict and a rebase. Check your progress in the lesson chip at the top.
